text.p: Belgian holding company Lonrho Continental said Lonrho Plc, its controlling shareholder, had agreed to sell its stake in the company to a group of Belgian investors.
Lonrho Plc held 82.48 percent of Lonrho Continental.

"The agreement provides for a price which is not greater than the average of the last 30 bourse quotations so that the conditions required for a public bid (for the remaining shares) are not met," Lonrho Continental said in a statement.
The firm did not specify which 30 days it meant.
In the past month Lonrho Continental has traded between 4,325 and 3,815 francs, valuing the stake at around 1.9 billion Belgian francs (32 million pounds sterling).
The deal should be completed in four weeks' time.
Lonrho Continental named the buyers as private merchant bank Bank Degroof and privately held companies Sofinim, Alva and 3D.
"Each investor will acquire between five and 12 percent of Lonrho Continental and a commonly-held company will acquire the remainder, that is around 30 percent," the company said.
The buyers planned to re-issue some of the acquired shares to the Brussels market, although no timescale had been fixed, Lonrho Continental said.
Lonrho Continental said the buying syndicate planned to maintain its property, trading and African businesses.
Lonrho Continental had 1996 profit of 154 million Belgian francs, up from 122 million in 1995.
